description: A measure across categories or over time, with the scale that says by how much: `type="bar"` for a value per category, `type="line"` for a value over time. Carries its own scale, grid, goal line, legend and hover readout, and reads as a TABLE to a screen reader. Reach for <Sparkline> when the shape sits beside a number and needs no axis, <DonutChart> for a whole split into named shares, <Meter> for one value against one target, and a <Table> when the numbers are compared exactly rather than at a glance. Copy: labels are the categories' or periods' own names, short enough to sit under a mark without turning. Series names are the things themselves, because a legend of "Series 1" is a legend of nothing. The accessible label says what is being counted and over what.

props.name: type
props.description: Which mark carries the data: `bar` for a value per category, `line` for a value over time. Everything else on this component is the same furniture.

props.name: labels
props.description: The categories, or the x axis oldest first: months, weeks, sites.

props.name: series
props.description: One entry per measure. Two or more bring a legend with them.

props.name: stacked
props.description: `bar`: segments of one column instead of columns side by side, for parts of a whole per period. Ignored with one series.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `bar`: bars run across instead of up. The answer for long category names and for a ranking, where the eye compares lengths down a column.

props.name: area
props.description: `line`: fills under the line. For ONE series only — two filled areas overlapping is a chart nobody can read.

props.name: max
props.description: Top of the scale. Defaults to the first nice number above the data; pass it when several charts must share one scale.

props.name: target
props.description: A goal drawn across the plot, so a value can be short OF something. Its own label is deliberately not a prop: a word printed inside the plot sits on the data (owner, 23.08). Name the goal in the card's meta line.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: `bar`: the one category that carries the accent — the current period, the site under discussion. Single-series only; the others stay quiet.

props.name: tone
props.description: What the whole measure MEANS, from the metric and not the numbers: findings closed rising is `success`, incidents rising is `danger`, and the same marks carry both.

props.name: size
props.description: How much of the page the chart is worth: `md` when it is the block, `sm` when it is one card in a grid of them.

props.name: axis
props.description: The scale down the side, and the grid lines with it. On by default: a mark with no scale is a shape, and the reader cannot say how big it is.

props.name: showValues
props.description: `bar`: values printed on every bar. Off by default — the readout under the pointer says it for the one being read, which is what a reader asks.

props.name: label
props.description: What the chart measures. Required in practice: it names the chart for a screen reader, which then reads the table this component renders for it.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP-47 tag for the numbers. Omit to follow the browser.
